text:
**Yes, but only some models can, and a basic one may drop your computer during an outage.**

## What to look for
- **Documented UPS/EPS mode with automatic switchover.** Anker says a power station can work as a UPS only if it has documented UPS or EPS functionality and automatic switchover. Otherwise it may keep appliances running but still interrupt a computer ([Anker](https://www.ankersolix.com/blogs/portable-power-station/can-a-portable-power-station-be-used-as-a-ups)).
- **Fast transfer time.** EcoFlow says many products advertise UPS backup but take 20-30 ms to switch, and it treats under 10 ms as the target for desktops and drives ([EcoFlow](https://www.ecoflow.com/us/blog/use-portable-power-station-as-ups-power-supply)). EcoFlow sells these products, so its claim that "9 times out of 10" the answer is no is a sales pitch, but the advice to check the spec is sound.
- **Pure sine wave output, pass-through support, and enough watts.** Add up your computer's real draw and compare it to the unit's continuous output rating.
- **Still not 0 ms.** Anker notes that 10 or 20 ms is not 0 ms, so check your computer's or NAS's manual. Strict loads like servers need an online double-conversion UPS ([Anker](https://www.ankersolix.com/blogs/home-power-backup/portable-power-station-ups-home-server-nas)).

## Runtime estimate
Runtime in hours ≈ Wh × 0.85 ÷ load in watts. A 1,000 Wh unit running a 100 W load gives about 8.5 hours at best, and real-world runtime is shorter.

## Models that publish UPS specs
- **[Anker SOLIX S2000](https://www.ankersolix.com/blogs/portable-power-station/can-a-portable-power-station-be-used-as-a-ups)**: 2,010 Wh, 1,500 W pure sine wave, 10 ms UPS switchover, listed at $699.99 after coupon.
- **[EcoFlow RIVER 3 Plus](https://www.ecoflow.com/us/blog/use-portable-power-station-as-ups-power-supply)**: under 10 ms switchover and 600 W output, which EcoFlow says is enough for a desktop and external drives. The same page says the DELTA Pro 3 offers UPS with 4,000 W output if you need more.

I couldn't confirm UPS switchover specs for the BLUETTI models in the results, so check their spec sheets before buying one for this purpose.

## Caveats
- A power station won't necessarily tell your PC to shut down safely. That needs UPS communication, which varies by model, so confirm it if you want automatic shutdown.
- If you only need a few minutes to save work and shut down, a standard desktop UPS is simpler and cheaper. A power station makes sense if you want hours of runtime.
